correctness.rationale: Complete midpoint classification of five-run Abelian-square factors, with b=d parity-band and b!=d endpoint cases, proves the exact formula. Direct factor-run classification bounds lower-run factors by 5n (at most four ambient runs) or 8n (five ambient runs). The continuous diagonal-band area lemma B(A,E,C)≤(A+E+C)^2/8 is proved in two exhaustive parameter regions, and a unit-square/parity comparison yields the global 1/16 upper coefficient. Explicit 0^(3m)1 0^(2m)1 0^(3m) provides 4m²+m five-run squares, and length extension proves the lower coefficient for all large lengths. Independent direct finite factor enumerations verified all 11,628 five-run words up to length 19, a 16,807-case parameter grid and 50 witness parameters. Finite checks corroborate, not prove, the infinite result.

originality.rationale: The exact five-run factor classification and sharp 1/16 extremal coefficient are not statements of the inspected Kociumaka–Radoszewski–Rytter–Waleń §2 (quadratic existence) or §3 (Abelian-inequivalent bounds); Fici–Mignosi–Shallit §3 likewise gives a quadratic construction but no sharp restricted coefficient. The two published five-run constructions have different, lower leading coefficients (3/64 and 1/18). Direct comparisons with the unrestricted OEIS table and targeted semantic searches did not identify coverage. This is best-knowledge originality, not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The exact threshold from linear to quadratic distinct Abelian-square complexity at five runs and its sharp leading coefficient resolve a natural restricted extremal problem suggested by the five-run constructions in arXiv:1604.02238 Fact 2.1 and arXiv:1701.00948 Proposition 1. The coefficient 1/16 improves the leading density of those existing witness shapes, and the exact 5-run factor classification identifies the mechanism of quadratic growth. This is a structural, infinite-length invariant rather than a table increment or arbitrary parameter slice.
